purpose: Test whether expansion from 16 to 34 BACE1 receptors makes the previously frozen seed-robust functional complementarity QUBO objective separate from a strong classical search while retaining scaffold-holdout utility.

evidence_timing.experiment_class: outcome-informed BACE1 train-only replication of a pre-BACE1 objective

objective.normalization: per-seed per-receptor empirical CDF fitted on the outer-train rows only

qubo_interpretation.receptor_variables: x_i=1 iff receptor i is selected
qubo_interpretation.active_auxiliaries: binary auxiliaries encode per-active per-seed single and double receptor support plus majority/all-seed thresholds
qubo_interpretation.decoy_auxiliaries: binary auxiliaries encode exposure by any selected receptor in any seed
qubo_interpretation.screen_solver: exact enumeration of every feasible receptor subset after analytically minimizing valid auxiliary relations
qubo_interpretation.claim_boundary: exact objective optimization is a QUBO upper-bound screen, not a quantum or annealing execution

required_comparators: beam-64 plus singleton multi-start plus add/drop/swap local search
exact optimum at each k from 1 through 6

support_gate.failure_action: Freeze this objective as unsupported on BACE1 and forbid weight retuning on the same BACE1 outcomes. Diagnose which objective component remains classically easy before any new experiment.

interpretation_boundary: Stage42d uses only the outcome-informed BACE1 Train-266 matrix and a functional objective frozen before BACE1 scores existed. A pass would justify sparse auxiliary-QUBO construction and one protected fresh-validation test; it would not establish independent multi-protein replication, quantum execution, or quantum advantage. A failure does not permit BACE1-specific weight tuning.
